cms2014_rows.name: cms2014_rows
cms2014_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition,
  provider_city AS city_raw,
  total_discharges,
  COALESCE(average_total_payments, average_medicare_payments, average_covered_charges) AS total_payments_or_avg_payment,
  provider_id AS hospital_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
grain: one row per row (each input row from 2014 inpatient shards)
cms2014_rows.description: Select all rows that belong to the 2014 CMS Medicare inpatient charges dataset (cohort filter). Keep raw fields needed for later aggregations such as drg_definition, city (un-normalized), total_discharges, and average_total_payments (or total_payments if present) and any hospital identifier.

normalized_fields.name: normalized_fields
normalized_fields.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Normalize DRG: trim whitespace and collapse internal multiple spaces to single, uppercase
  REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(drg_definition)), r'\s+', ' ') AS drg_definition_norm,
  -- Normalize city: uppercase, trim, collapse spaces (canonical for grouping)
  REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(provider_city)), r'\s+', ' ') AS city_norm,
  -- Ensure total_discharges is numeric: coerce NULLs to 0 (keep as INT64)
  SAFE_CAST(total_discharges AS INT64) AS total_discharges_num,
  -- Compute total_payments_num:
  -- Prefer an explicit 'average_total_payments' * total_discharges when total_payments not provided.
  -- If there's an explicit total_payments field in source, use it; otherwise compute from average.
  COALESCE(
    SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(CAST(NULL AS STRING), '') AS FLOAT64), -- placeholder if source had total_payments column (none in DDL)
    SAFE_CAST(average_total_payments AS FLOAT64) * SAFE_CAST(total_discharges AS FLOAT64)
  ) AS total_payments_num,
  -- Row identity: combine table suffix + provider_id + row number for uniqueness within shard
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '_', provider_id, '_', CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY _TABLE_SUFFIX ORDER BY provider_id, drg_definition, provider_city) AS STRING)) AS row_id,
  -- Preserve hospital identifier
  provider_id AS hospital_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
grain: one row per row_id (constructed as shard_suffix + provider_id + per-shard row number)
normalized_fields.description: Canonicalize and project fields from the selected rows: trim and standardize drg_definition string, normalize city names to a canonical form for case-insensitive grouping, and ensure numeric types for total_discharges and total_payments (or compute total_payments if only avg provided and discharges available). Preserve hospital_id and original row identity.

drg_total_discharges.name: drg_total_discharges
drg_total_discharges.body_sql:
SELECT
  UPPER(TRIM(drg_definition)) AS drg_definition_norm,
  SUM(COALESCE(total_discharges,0)) AS drg_total_discharges
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
  AND drg_definition IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  drg_definition_norm
drg_total_discharges.description: Compute total discharges aggregated across all rows for each DRG definition (sum of total_discharges_num) to identify which DRG definition has the largest overall discharge volume.

prescriptions_2014_sel.name: prescriptions_2014_sel
prescriptions_2014_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.nppes_provider_state AS state,
  p.drug_name AS medication,
  -- Use total_claim_count as the prescription_row_count when available; fall back to 1 per row
  COALESCE(p.total_claim_count, 1) AS prescription_row_count,
  -- construct a stable prescription_id at the row level using available fields (npi + drug_name + state + total_day_supply)
  -- keep as string so it's joinable; callers can hash if needed
  CONCAT(p.npi, '::', SAFE_CAST(p.total_day_supply AS STRING), '::', p.drug_name, '::', p.nppes_provider_state) AS prescription_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014` AS p
WHERE
  p.nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
  AND p.drug_name IS NOT NULL
  -- restrict to year 2014 data source (table is specifically 2014); keep literal pulled out of view if needed
  -- no additional date filtering needed because table is the 2014 dataset
prescriptions_2014_sel.description: Select prescription rows for year 2014 with a valid U.S. state value; keep medication identifier/name and count of a single prescription row (or preserve prescription quantity if present) for later aggregation.

state_medication_counts_agg.name: state_medication_counts_agg
state_medication_counts_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  drug_name AS medication,
  -- prefer summed total_claim_count when available; otherwise fall back to counting rows
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(total_claim_count) IS NOT NULL THEN SUM(total_claim_count)
    ELSE COUNT(1)
  END AS prescription_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  nppes_provider_state,
  drug_name
state_medication_counts_agg.description: Aggregate prescription rows to compute total prescriptions per medication within each state (sum of prescription_row_count or count of rows if row-level quantity not available).

state_max_count_agg.name: state_max_count_agg
state_max_count_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  MAX(total_claim_count) AS max_prescription_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
GROUP BY
  nppes_provider_state
state_max_count_agg.description: For each state, compute the maximum prescription_count across medications (one row per state with that max value).

top_medications_per_state_join.name: top_medications_per_state_join
top_medications_per_state_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  smc.`state` AS state,
  smc.`medication` AS medication,
  smc.`prescription_count` AS prescription_count
FROM
  -- per-state, per-medication counts (reuse of state_medication_counts_agg if available)
  `state_medication_counts_agg` AS smc
JOIN
  `state_max_count_agg` AS smm
ON smc.`state` = smm.`state`
AND smc.`prescription_count` = smm.`max_prescription_count`
ORDER BY smc.`state`, smc.`medication`
top_medications_per_state_join.description: Join medication-level counts with the per-state maximums to retain medications whose prescription_count equals the state's max, producing one row per tied top medication per state; final relation can be ordered by state.

provider_combined_average_2014.name: provider_combined_average_2014
provider_combined_average_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(o.provider_id, i.provider_id) AS provider_id,
  -- outpatient average per provider in 2014: average of average_total_payments from outpatient_charges_2014
  o.outpatient_avg_2014 AS outpatient_avg_2014,
  -- inpatient average per provider in 2014: average of average_covered_charges from inpatient_charges_2014
  i.inpatient_avg_2014 AS inpatient_avg_2014,
  -- combined as sum (NULLs preserved; consumers can filter to require both present)
  CASE
    WHEN o.outpatient_avg_2014 IS NULL AND i.inpatient_avg_2014 IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE COALESCE(o.outpatient_avg_2014, 0) + COALESCE(i.inpatient_avg_2014, 0)
  END AS combined_average_cost_2014
FROM
  (
    -- aggregate outpatient per provider for 2014
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      AVG(average_total_payments) AS outpatient_avg_2014
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_2014`
    GROUP BY
      provider_id
  ) AS o
FULL JOIN
  (
    -- aggregate inpatient per provider for 2014
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      AVG(average_covered_charges) AS inpatient_avg_2014
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_2014`
    GROUP BY
      provider_id
  ) AS i
USING (provider_id)
provider_combined_average_2014.description: Reshape/pivot the per-provider per-service averages into one row per provider with separate columns for outpatient and inpatient average costs, then compute combined_average_cost_2014 = outpatient_avg + inpatient_avg. Do not filter out missing values here (filtering for both present happens in final step).

claims_2014_us_states.name: claims_2014_us_states
claims_2014_us_states.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- drug identifier: prefer generic_name when available, else drug_name
  COALESCE(`generic_name`, `drug_name`) AS drug_id,
  -- state (2-letter postal/state code)
  `nppes_provider_state` AS state_id,
  -- claim count and drug cost aggregated per prescriber-drug-state claim record
  SUM(`total_claim_count`) AS claim_count,
  SUM(`total_drug_cost`) AS drug_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
-- restrict to calendar year 2014 rows (table is the 2014 table) and US states:
-- keep rows where state looks like a 2-letter postal code (A-Z) and not NULL
WHERE
  `nppes_provider_state` IS NOT NULL
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(`nppes_provider_state`, r'^[A-Z]{2}$')
  AND (`drug_name` IS NOT NULL OR `generic_name` IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(`generic_name`, `drug_name`),
  `nppes_provider_state`
grain: one row per prescriber-drug-state aggregate claim_record
claims_2014_us_states.description: Select all prescription claim records for calendar year 2014 that are located in U.S. states (restrict geography to U.S. states). Keep relevant fields for drug identifier, state, claim count and drug cost.

ny_state_claims_by_drug.name: ny_state_claims_by_drug
ny_state_claims_by_drug.body_sql:
SELECT
  drug_name AS drug_id,
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS ny_total_claim_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
GROUP BY
  drug_name
ny_state_claims_by_drug.description: Aggregate the 2014 U.S. state claims to compute total claim counts per drug specifically for New York State. One row per drug with its sum of claim counts in New York.

provider_year_row_costs.name: provider_year_row_costs
provider_year_row_costs.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.provider_id AS provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  SAFE_MULTIPLY(i.average_medicare_payments, i.total_discharges) AS inpatient_cost,
  -- outpatient_cost: use average_total_payments * outpatient_services.
  -- There is no outpatient_services column in inpatient_charges tables; lift outpatient_services literal (NULL) out of view by computing NULL if missing.
  -- If a caller can provide outpatient_services via join later, they should do so; here we compute outpatient_cost when average_total_payments and outpatient_services are present.
  CASE
    WHEN i.average_total_payments IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE NULL
  END AS outpatient_cost
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*` AS i
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
provider_year_row_costs.description: For each input row, compute the per-row inpatient_cost as (average_medicare_payments * total_discharges) and per-row outpatient_cost as (average_total_payments * outpatient_services); keep original provider and year keys so each source row remains one output row.

provider_year_averages.name: provider_year_averages
provider_year_averages.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
  AVG(average_total_payments) AS avg_yearly_inpatient_cost,
  AVG(average_covered_charges) AS avg_yearly_outpatient_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
provider_year_averages.description: For each provider and calendar year, compute the yearly average inpatient cost as the average of inpatient_cost across that provider-year's rows, and yearly average outpatient cost as the average of outpatient_cost across that provider-year's rows.
counter_examples: For the provider whose total inpatient Medicare cost from 2011 through 2015 is the highest (computed as the sum of average_medicare_payments multiplied by total_discharges), please list that provider’s yearly average inpatient cost and yearly average outpatient cost for each calendar year in this period, where the inpatient cost is calculated as the average of (average_medicare_payments × total_discharges) and the outpatient cost is calculated as the average of (average_total_payments × outpatient_services).

person_population.name: person_population
person_population.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.`person_id`
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
GROUP BY
  p.`person_id`
person_population.description: All distinct persons (participants) in the dataset to form the denominator; one row per person.

target_standard_concepts.name: target_standard_concepts
target_standard_concepts.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a canonical identifier: prefer OMOP concept_id when available, otherwise ICD-10-CM code string
  COALESCE(CAST(c.concept_id AS STRING), d.cm_code) AS condition_standard_concept_id_or_code,
  -- human readable name: prefer OMOP concept_name when available, otherwise ICD short_description
  COALESCE(c.concept_name, d.short_description) AS condition_standard_concept_name
FROM (
  -- ICD-10-CM source: restrict to the four target top-level codes (lift literals out of downstream code)
  SELECT cm_code, short_description
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019`
  WHERE cm_code IN ('L70','L20','L40','L80')
) AS d
LEFT JOIN (
  -- OMOP concept table: find matching concept(s) by exact code text or name containing the condition term.
  -- We join on name or code match so that when an OMOP standard concept exists we can surface its id and preferred name.
  SELECT concept_id, concept_name, LOWER(concept_name) AS concept_name_lc, concept_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept`
  WHERE LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%acne%'
     OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%atopic%'
     OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%psoriasis%'
     OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%vitiligo%'
     OR concept_code IN ('L70','L20','L40','L80')
) AS c
ON (
  -- match by exact ICD code present as concept_code OR by name similarity between ICD short_description and OMOP concept_name
  c.concept_code = d.cm_code
  OR LOWER(d.short_description) = c.concept_name_lc
)
target_standard_concepts.description: The four standard ICD-10-CM target concepts (acne L70, atopic dermatitis L20, psoriasis L40, vitiligo L80) expressed as one row per standard concept; used as roots for descendant expansion. This relation lists the canonical identifier/code and human-readable name for each standard concept.

participants_base_cohort.name: participants_base_cohort
participants_base_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(p.person_id AS INT64) AS participant_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
participants_base_cohort.description: Select the set of participants to consider. If the schema has an active/inactive participant flag, filter to active participants; otherwise include all participants.

medication_records_rxcui_norm.name: medication_records_rxcui_norm
medication_records_rxcui_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key columns carried through so view is joinable
  de.drug_exposure_id AS medication_id,
  de.person_id AS participant_id,

  -- Normalize/canonicalize RxCUI:
  -- Prefer explicit OMOP drug_concept_id when it represents an RxNorm concept.
  -- If drug_concept_id is present use it; otherwise try to coerce drug_source_value or drug_source_concept_id.
  -- Ensure integer output: CAST to INT64 when possible; NULL when not parseable.
  -- Lift any question-specific literal out of the view (none used here).
  (
    CASE
      WHEN de.drug_concept_id IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(de.drug_concept_id AS INT64)
      WHEN SAFE_CAST(de.drug_source_concept_id AS INT64) IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(de.drug_source_concept_id AS INT64)
      WHEN de.drug_source_value IS NOT NULL THEN
        -- try to extract digits from drug_source_value and cast; if non-numeric, result will be NULL
        SAFE_CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(de.drug_source_value, r'[^0-9]+', '') AS INT64)
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS rxcui

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` AS de
medication_records_rxcui_norm.description: Project and canonicalize medication records to expose medication identifier fields including an integer RxCUI; ensure RxCUI is cast/normalized to an integer for exact matching.

participants_with_quinapril.name: participants_with_quinapril
participants_with_quinapril.body_sql:
SELECT
  person_id AS participant_id,
  IF(COUNTIF(drug_concept_id = 35208) > 0, TRUE, FALSE) AS uses_quinapril_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
GROUP BY
  person_id
participants_with_quinapril.description: For each participant, determine whether they have any medication record whose normalized rxcui equals 35208. Produce one row per participant with a flag indicating quinapril use.

quinapril_usage_summary.name: quinapril_usage_summary
quinapril_usage_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  'aggregate_row' AS aggregate_row,
  -- total distinct participants in cohort (lift literal out of view: none)
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) AS total_participants,
  -- count of participants who do NOT have any quinapril drug_exposure (quinapril identified by drug_source_value or drug_concept_id left to query-time mapping)
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN de.person_id IS NOT NULL THEN p.person_id END) AS count_not_using_quinapril,
  -- percentage not using quinapril (as float). Percentage = 100 * count_not_using_quinapril / total_participants
  SAFE_DIVIDE(100.0 * (COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN de.person_id IS NOT NULL THEN p.person_id END)), NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id), 0)) AS percentage_not_using_quinapril
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
LEFT JOIN (
  -- quinapril exposures: identify by drug_source_value containing 'quinapril' (case-insensitive).
  SELECT DISTINCT person_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
  WHERE LOWER(COALESCE(drug_source_value, '')) LIKE '%quinapril%'
) AS de
ON p.person_id = de.person_id
quinapril_usage_summary.description: Combine the participant cohort with the per-participant quinapril-usage flag to compute counts: total participants, count not using quinapril, and percentage not using quinapril.

tracks_in_basin_year.name: tracks_in_basin_year
tracks_in_basin_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(sid, '-', CAST(number AS STRING)) AS hurricane_id,
  iso_time AS track_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  basin,
  CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM iso_time) AS INT64) AS year,
  CASE WHEN LOWER(usa_status) IN ('hu','hr','ty','tc','st') OR (COALESCE(usa_wind, 0) >= 64) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_hurricane_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE
  basin = 'NA'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM iso_time) = 2020
  AND (
    LOWER(usa_status) IN ('hu','hr','ty','tc','st')
    OR COALESCE(usa_wind, 0) >= 64
  )
tracks_in_basin_year.description: Select all track points for cyclones that are classified as hurricanes and that occur in the North Atlantic basin during the calendar year 2020. Each row is an individual track observation with its timestamp and geographic coordinates.

stations_period_filter.name: stations_period_filter
stations_period_filter.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stations.usaf, '-', stations.wban) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.begin) AS period_of_record_start_date,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.`end`) AS period_of_record_end_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS stations
WHERE
  -- Lifted literals: cutoff_start_date and cutoff_end_date should be provided by the query using this view.
  -- Here we enforce that station begin <= cutoff_start_date AND station end >= cutoff_end_date.
  -- Replace @cutoff_start_date and @cutoff_end_date (DATE) when querying the view.
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.begin) <= @cutoff_start_date
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.`end`) >= @cutoff_end_date
stations_period_filter.description: Subset of NOAA GSOD stations whose period-of-record begins on or before a cutoff date and continues through at least an end cutoff date. This filters stations eligible for 2019-based evaluation based on their period start and end.

daily_temperature_flags_2019.name: daily_temperature_flags_2019
daily_temperature_flags_2019.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- station identifier: concatenate stn and wban when available to form station_id
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(wban, '') = '' THEN stn
    ELSE CONCAT(stn, '-', wban)
  END AS station_id,
  -- date in YYYY-MM-DD from year/mo/da (gsod tables use string year/mo/da)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  -- raw temperature fields (mean, max, min) as provided
  temp AS temperature,
  max AS max_temperature,
  min AS min_temperature,
  -- valid day if none of temp/max/min are the missing sentinel values (9999.9)
  CASE
    WHEN temp IS NOT NULL AND max IS NOT NULL AND min IS NOT NULL
     AND temp != 9999.9 AND max != 9999.9 AND min != 9999.9 THEN TRUE
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS is_valid_temp_day_2019
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- restrict to year 2019 using _TABLE_SUFFIX for wildcard sharded tables
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2019'
  -- ensure the parsed date is in calendar year 2019 (defensive)
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE('2019-01-01') AND DATE('2019-12-31')
daily_temperature_flags_2019.description: One row per station-day in calendar year 2019 with indicators showing whether that day's temperature, max, and min values are all present (i.e., a valid temperature-record day). Include the date and raw temperature-related fields for potential cleaning.

daily_observations.name: daily_observations
daily_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- station identifier (keep original station id column name)
  stn AS station_id,
  -- observation_date: construct DATE from year, month, day (gsod uses year/mo/da as strings)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS observation_date,
  -- temperature: daily mean temp in Fahrenheit (temp field), treat missing 9999.9 as NULL
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS temperature,
  -- wind_speed: mean wind speed for the day in knots in GSOD (wdsp), convert to FLOAT and treat 999.9 as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) = 999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64)
  END AS wind_speed,
  -- precipitation: daily total precipitation in inches (prcp), treat 99.99 as NULL
  NULLIF(prcp, 99.99) AS precipitation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- keep only June 12 of each year: month = '06' and day = '12'
  mo = '06'
  AND da = '12'
  -- restrict shards to a reasonable range if needed (lifted literal: years of interest)
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  -- exclude rows with no station id or invalid parsed date
  AND stn IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) IS NOT NULL
daily_observations.description: Select raw observation records for all dates of interest (June 12 for each year). This is a row-level cohort filtered by station and date range but does not aggregate; keep measured fields as-is (temperature, wind_speed, precipitation) and the observation date.

non_null_wind_rows.name: non_null_wind_rows
non_null_wind_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- source table identifier
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_name,
  -- construct ISO date from year, month, day; keep NULL if any component NULL
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS date,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  -- daily average wind speed: keep same units as source (do not introduce literals). Nulls will be filtered by outer view consumer.
  wind_speed AS daily_avg_wind_speed,
  -- raw_row_id: compose a stable identifier from shard suffix + position columns so rows remain joinable
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '::', CAST(COALESCE(CAST(year AS STRING),'') AS STRING), '-', CAST(COALESCE(CAST(month AS STRING),'') AS STRING), '-', CAST(COALESCE(CAST(day AS STRING),'') AS STRING), '::', CAST(COALESCE(CAST(hour AS STRING),'') AS STRING), '::', CAST(COALESCE(CAST(latitude AS STRING),'') AS STRING), '::', CAST(COALESCE(CAST(longitude AS STRING),'') AS STRING)) AS raw_row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  -- restrict to the known shards range as instructed; lift literals out as parameters if needed
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2005' AND '2017'
  -- Keep only rows where the daily average wind speed is not NULL (per spec: exclude NULL daily avg wind)
  AND wind_speed IS NOT NULL
non_null_wind_rows.description: Filter the normalized rows to exclude any rows where the daily average wind speed is NULL, keeping one row per original observation.

station_day_validity.name: station_day_validity
station_day_validity.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf AS usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(g.year, '-', LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(g.da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  TRUE AS has_any_observation_day,
  -- determine valid temperature day: temp, max, and min are NOT the missing sentinels (9999.9) and NOT NULL
  (
    SAFE_CAST(g.temp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(g.temp AS FLOAT64) != 9999.9
    AND SAFE_CAST(g.max AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(g.max AS FLOAT64) != 9999.9
    AND SAFE_CAST(g.min AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(g.min AS FLOAT64) != 9999.9
  ) AS is_valid_temperature_day
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
ON
  g.stn = s.usaf
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2022' AND '2022'
  -- restrict to rows that parse to a valid 2022 date to avoid malformed shards/rows
  AND SAFE_CAST(g.year AS INT64) = 2022
station_day_validity.description: For each station and calendar date in 2022 for which the station has any observation, determine whether that day counts as a valid-temperature-day (true if temp_clean, max_temp_clean, and min_temp_clean are all non-null for at least one observation on that date for the station). Also include a flag that the station had any observation that day (the denominator membership).

station_locations.name: station_locations
station_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stations.usaf, '-', stations.wban) AS station_id,
  stations.name AS station_name,
  stations.state AS state
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS stations
station_locations.description: All weather station records with their canonical station identifier and state/country location fields (one row per station). This isolates the station cohort to be filtered to Washington in a later step.

rainy_days_per_station_year.name: rainy_days_per_station_year
rainy_days_per_station_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(COALESCE(stn, ''), IFNULL(NULLIF(wban, ''), '')) AS station_id,
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0')) AS DATE)) AS rainy_days
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  -- valid precipitation: prcp is not the missing sentinel 99.99 and not null
  AND prcp IS NOT NULL
  AND prcp != 99.99
  -- interpret a rainy day as any day with reported precipitation > 0.00
  AND prcp > 0.00
  -- carry key columns for joinability
GROUP BY station_id, year
rainy_days_per_station_year.description: Aggregate cleaned observations to count distinct rainy days per station and year. Each row is one station-year with the count of days where is_rainy is true and only using valid precipitation records.

daily_country_aggregates.name: daily_country_aggregates
daily_country_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.country AS country_code,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(g.year, '-', LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(g.da,2,'0'))) AS observation_date,
  MAX(NULLIF(g.max, 9999.9)) AS day_max_temperature,
  MIN(NULLIF(g.min, 9999.9)) AS day_min_temperature,
  AVG(NULLIF(g.temp, 9999.9)) AS day_avg_temperature
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
ON
  g.stn = s.usaf
  AND ( (g.wban IS NULL AND s.wban IS NULL) OR (g.wban = s.wban) )
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  -- exclude missing sentinel values in joins/filters by using NULLIF in aggregates
GROUP BY
  country_code,
  observation_date
daily_country_aggregates.description: For each country and calendar date, compute per-day aggregates (maximum, minimum, and average) from valid station numeric temperatures. One row per country-date with the three aggregate measures.

rochester_daily_observations.name: rochester_daily_observations
rochester_daily_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- obs_date: assemble from GSOD year/mo/da (strings in source) into DATE; keep as DATE type
  DATE(CAST(g.year AS INT64), CAST(g.mo AS INT64), CAST(g.da AS INT64)) AS obs_date,

  -- location: use station id as "stn-wban" to keep joinable identifier and location notion
  CONCAT(g.stn, '-', g.wban) AS location,

  -- temperature: keep original units as stored in gsod (degrees Fahrenheit to tenths; missing = 9999.9)
  g.temp AS temperature,

  -- precipitation: keep original units as stored in gsod (inches and hundredths; missing = 99.99)
  g.prcp AS precipitation,

  -- wind_speed: keep original units as stored in gsod (knots to tenths in wdsp; sometimes stored as STRING -> cast when possible)
  -- preserve NULL when value is missing or unparsable; do NOT convert units
  SAFE_CAST(g.wdsp AS FLOAT64) AS wind_speed,

  -- carry original station components so the view remains joinable (grain requires obs_date + location; these are present)
  g.stn AS stn,
  g.wban AS wban
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
-- Do not apply any _TABLE_SUFFIX clipping here per instruction; users will filter when querying the view.
-- Restrict nothing else so the full available period is represented.
rochester_daily_observations.description: Select daily raw weather observations (date, station/location, temperature, precipitation, wind speed) for Rochester for the full available period; do not apply date-range clipping here. Keep original units as stored.

new_users_2021.name: new_users_2021
new_users_2021.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  creation_date AS creation_timestamp,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP("%Y-%m", creation_date) AS creation_month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
WHERE
  creation_date >= TIMESTAMP("2021-01-01T00:00:00Z")
  AND creation_date < TIMESTAMP("2022-01-01T00:00:00Z")
new_users_2021.description: All users whose account creation timestamp falls within the inclusive 2021 calendar range. Keep each user and their creation timestamp and a canonical month key (year-month) derived from creation timestamp.

questions_within_30d.name: questions_within_30d
questions_within_30d.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
ON
  q.owner_user_id = u.id
WHERE
  -- question created within 30 days (0-30 days) on-or-after the user's creation timestamp
  q.creation_date BETWEEN u.creation_date AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(u.creation_date, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
questions_within_30d.description: Question posts that occur within 30 days on-or-after a user's creation timestamp. Each row links a question to its author (user) and includes question creation timestamp; used to determine whether a new user asked within 30 days and to find the user's first question within that window.

answers_after_first_within_30d.name: answers_after_first_within_30d
answers_after_first_within_30d.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.owner_user_id AS user_id,
  a.id AS answer_id,
  a.creation_date AS answer_creation_timestamp,
  fq.first_question_timestamp AS first_question_timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
JOIN (
  -- first question timestamp per user from questions table
  SELECT
    q.owner_user_id AS user_id,
    MIN(q.creation_date) AS first_question_timestamp
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
  WHERE q.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY q.owner_user_id
) AS fq
ON a.owner_user_id = fq.user_id
WHERE
  a.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  AND a.creation_date IS NOT NULL
  -- answers posted after the first question and within 30 days after it
  AND a.creation_date > fq.first_question_timestamp
  AND a.creation_date <= TIMESTAMP_ADD(fq.first_question_timestamp, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
answers_after_first_within_30d.description: Answers posted by the same user after their first question and within 30 days after that first question. Each row links an answer to the user and the first-question timestamp to allow boolean determination per user whether they answered in that window.

questions_base.name: questions_base
questions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  creation_date AS question_creation_ts
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 1
questions_base.description: All rows representing questions with their primary key and creation timestamp; one row per question as recorded in the questions source.

answers_earliest_per_question.name: answers_earliest_per_question
answers_earliest_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  MIN(creation_date) AS earliest_answer_ts
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
GROUP BY
  question_id
answers_earliest_per_question.description: For each question that has any answers, the earliest answer creation timestamp (one row per question).

answer_posts.name: answer_posts
answer_posts.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS post_id,
  owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
answer_posts.description: Select all post records that are answers (exclude questions); keep the post id and the owner/user id for each answer.

eligible_users.name: eligible_users
eligible_users.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  display_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
WHERE
  reputation > 10
eligible_users.description: Select users who meet the reputation filter (reputation > 10); keep user id and display name.

user_answer_counts.name: user_answer_counts
user_answer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(owner_user_id AS INT64) AS user_id,
  COUNT(1) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  owner_user_id
user_answer_counts.description: Aggregate the answers relation to count the number of answers per user (one row per user who has at least one answer).

eligible_user_counts.name: eligible_user_counts
eligible_user_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  u.display_name AS display_name,
  COUNT(a.id) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
ON
  a.owner_user_id = u.id
GROUP BY
  u.id,
  u.display_name
HAVING
  COUNT(a.id) > 0
eligible_user_counts.description: Join eligible users to their answer counts to produce one row per eligible user with display name and answer_count (users with no answers should be excluded by using the counts relation).

post_questions_only.name: post_questions_only
post_questions_only.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS post_id,
  title,
  body,
  tags,
  answer_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE post_type_id = 1
  AND tags LIKE '%<python-2>%'
post_questions_only.description: Select only posts that are actual questions (exclude answers and comments) with their identifiers and raw fields needed for tagging/text filters and answer counts.

python2_specific_questions.name: python2_specific_questions
python2_specific_questions.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS post_id,
  title,
  body,
  tags,
  answer_count,
  -- indicator: 1 if tags or title/body mention Python 2 (python-2 or python-2.x or "python 2" textual), else 0
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(tags), r'(^|<|;)python-2(\.|$|>)')
      OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(tags), r'(^|<|;)python-2\.7(\.|$|>)')
      OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(title), r'(?i)\bpython[\s\-]?2(\.\d+)?\b')
      OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(body), r'(?i)\bpython[\s\-]?2(\.\d+)?\b')
      THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS python2_indicator
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 1
  AND (
    REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(tags), r'(^|<|;)python-2(\.|$|>)')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(tags), r'(^|<|;)python-2\.7(\.|$|>)')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(title), r'(?i)\bpython[\s\-]?2(\.\d+)?\b')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(body), r'(?i)\bpython[\s\-]?2(\.\d+)?\b')
  )
python2_specific_questions.description: Filter the questions to those that are specifically about Python 2 (e.g., have a python-2.x tag or text indicating Python 2 specificity) — but do not yet exclude Python 3 mentions. Keep original text/tags for later exclusion.
counter_examples: What is the highest number of answers received for a single Python 2 specific question on Stack Overflow, excluding any discussions that involve Python 3?

max_answers_per_question.name: max_answers_per_question
max_answers_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  MAX(p.answer_count) AS max_answers
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS p
WHERE
  -- Python-2-only questions are indicated by the presence of the tag 'python-2'
  -- and absence of the tag 'python-3' in the tags string.
  -- Tags are stored as a single string like "<python-2><pandas>" so we search for substrings.
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(p.tags, r'(^|<)python-2(>|<)') 
  AND NOT REGEXP_CONTAINS(p.tags, r'(^|<)python-3(>|<)')
max_answers_per_question.description: Compute the maximum answer_count across the remaining Python-2-only questions. One row per question is preserved in input; this relation produces the aggregate maximum value as a single-row result.

questions_jan2016_with_tags.name: questions_jan2016_with_tags
questions_jan2016_with_tags.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(creation_date, DAY) AS question_post_date,
  tags AS question_tags,
  score AS question_score,
  answer_count AS question_answer_count,
  view_count AS question_view_count,
  comment_count AS question_comment_count,
  owner_user_id AS asker_user_id,
  accepted_answer_id AS question_accepted_answer_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(creation_date, MONTH) = TIMESTAMP("2016-01-01")
  AND LOWER(tags) LIKE '%javascript%'
  AND (
    LOWER(tags) LIKE '%xss%'
    OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%cross-site%'
    OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%exploit%'
    OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%cybersecurity%'
  )
questions_jan2016_with_tags.description: Select questions posted in January 2016 whose tag set includes 'javascript' and at least one of the security-related tags ('xss','cross-site','exploit','cybersecurity'). Keep question-level metadata needed later.

users_basic.name: users_basic
users_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  reputation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
users_basic.description: Select user basic info (user_id and reputation) for asked and answering users to allow joining reputations.

questions_2022_sel.name: questions_2022_sel
questions_2022_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS post_id,
  creation_date,
  tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  -- questions only and created within 2022 inclusive
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2022
questions_2022_sel.description: Select all posts that are questions created within the 2022 date range (inclusive). Do not collapse rows; keep each question as one row with its creation timestamp and tags string/array and post id.

questions_normalized_tags.name: questions_normalized_tags
questions_normalized_tags.body_sql:
-- View body: one row per question-tag (normalized to lowercase, trimmed)
SELECT
  id AS post_id,
  creation_date,
  LOWER(TRIM(tag)) AS tag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`,
  UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(IFNULL(tags, ''), r'[<>]', ' '), ' ')) AS tag
WHERE
  tags IS NOT NULL
  AND tags != ''
  AND TRIM(tag) != ''
questions_normalized_tags.description: Normalize/clean tags for each question row (e.g., lowercasing, split tag string into individual tag rows or canonical array) so tag membership tests (case-insensitive) are straightforward. Keep one row per question-tag if expanding, or keep per-question with a normalized tag array.

questions_monthly_flagged.name: questions_monthly_flagged
questions_monthly_flagged.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS post_id,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%F', TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(q.creation_date, MONTH)) AS month,
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(tag) = 'python' THEN TRUE
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS is_python
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(SPLIT(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(q.tags, '<', ''), '>', ' '), '  ', ' '))) AS tag
questions_monthly_flagged.description: For each question-tag row, compute the month of the question (format YYYY-MM) and flag whether the tag equals 'python' (case-insensitive). Keep one row per question (or per question-month) while preserving the python-flag for later aggregation.

user_contributions_raw.name: user_contributions_raw
user_contributions_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- questions authored by users
  'question' AS contrib_type,
  q.id AS contrib_id,
  q.creation_date AS created_at,
  q.owner_user_id AS user_id,
  q.id AS question_id,
  NULL AS answer_id,
  NULL AS parent_post_id,
  NULL AS parent_post_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE
  q.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT
  -- answers authored by users (keep link to parent question)
  'answer' AS contrib_type,
  a.id AS contrib_id,
  a.creation_date AS created_at,
  a.owner_user_id AS user_id,
  a.parent_id AS question_id,
  a.id AS answer_id,
  NULL AS parent_post_id,
  NULL AS parent_post_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  a.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT
  -- comments authored by users (link to parent post and its type)
  'comment' AS contrib_type,
  c.id AS contrib_id,
  c.creation_date AS created_at,
  c.user_id AS user_id,
  -- attempt to place comment's question_id and answer_id as NULL here;
  -- parent_post_id and parent_post_type carry the linkage
  NULL AS question_id,
  NULL AS answer_id,
  c.post_id AS parent_post_id,
  -- parent_post_type is unknown from comments table; infer as 'question'/'answer' if possible by checking posts tables
  CASE
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` pq WHERE pq.id = c.post_id
    ) THEN 'question'
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` pa WHERE pa.id = c.post_id
    ) THEN 'answer'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS parent_post_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments` AS c
WHERE
  c.user_id IS NOT NULL
user_contributions_raw.description: All user-authored contribution rows (questions, answers, comments) restricted to the contributor ID range and date range. Each row identifies the contribution type, its own id, creation datetime, the author user_id, and linkage keys to the related question or parent answer as available (for answers keep parent_question_id; for comments keep parent_post_id and parent_post_type or parent_answer_id).

answers_with_question.name: answers_with_question
answers_with_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS answer_id,
  parent_id AS parent_question_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  -- only include rows that are answers (post_type_id = 2 is conventional for answers in StackOverflow schema)
  post_type_id = 2
  -- keep only non-null parent pointers
  AND parent_id IS NOT NULL
answers_with_question.description: For answer contributions, the mapping from an answer id to its parent question id. One row per answer containing answer id and its parent question id.

questions_with_tags.name: questions_with_tags
questions_with_tags.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS user_id,
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.tags AS question_tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
questions_with_tags.description: Each question with its stored tag representation (the tag set/string/collection used by the schema). One row per question with question id and its tags.

contributions_with_question_tags.name: contributions_with_question_tags
contributions_with_question_tags.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- contribution type: 'question', 'answer', or 'comment'
  contrib_type,
  -- contribution id (question.id, answer.id, or comment.id)
  contrib_id,
  -- user who made the contribution (may be NULL for anonymous)
  user_id,
  -- contribution creation timestamp
  created_at,
  -- canonical question id for this contribution
  question_id,
  -- tags string from the question row
  question_tags
FROM (
  -- Questions: use question rows directly
  SELECT
    'question' AS contrib_type,
    q.id AS contrib_id,
    q.owner_user_id AS user_id,
    q.creation_date AS created_at,
    q.id AS question_id,
    q.tags AS question_tags
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q

  UNION ALL

  -- Answers: map answer -> parent question_id using parent_id in answers table
  SELECT
    'answer' AS contrib_type,
    a.id AS contrib_id,
    a.owner_user_id AS user_id,
    a.creation_date AS created_at,
    a.parent_id AS question_id,
    q.tags AS question_tags
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
    ON a.parent_id = q.id

  UNION ALL

  -- Comments: if comment.post_id refers to a question use it directly,
  -- otherwise if it refers to an answer, join answers to get its parent question.
  SELECT
    'comment' AS contrib_type,
    c.id AS contrib_id,
    c.user_id AS user_id,
    c.creation_date AS created_at,
    -- resolve comment's question id: prefer question.id if post is a question, else answer.parent_id
    COALESCE(q.id, a.parent_id) AS question_id,
    COALESCE(q.tags, q_from_answer.tags) AS question_tags
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments` AS c
  -- try to join comment.post_id to questions
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
    ON c.post_id = q.id
  -- try to join comment.post_id to answers
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
    ON c.post_id = a.id
  -- join the question for that answer (if any) to get tags
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q_from_answer
    ON a.parent_id = q_from_answer.id
)
contributions_with_question_tags.description: For every contribution row (question, answer, or comment) produce one row that associates the contribution to the relevant question_id and attaches that question's tags. Uses question rows directly for question contributions; uses answer->question mapping for answer contributions; for comments, resolves whether the comment's parent is a question (use that question_id) or an answer (use the answer's parent_question_id).

candidate_questions_text_filtered.name: candidate_questions_text_filtered
candidate_questions_text_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  title,
  body,
  view_count,
  creation_date,
  score,
  answer_count,
  tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  -- include rows where title OR body contains the whole word 'how' (case-insensitive)
  (
    REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(title, '')), r'(?m)(?:\bhow\b)')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(body, '')), r'(?m)(?:\bhow\b)')
  )
  -- exclude rows where EITHER title OR body contain any troubleshooting whole-word terms (case-insensitive)
  AND NOT (
    REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(title, '')), r'(?m)(?:\btroubleshoot\b|\btroubleshooting\b|\berror\b|\bfailure\b|\bbug\b|\bissue\b|\bproblem\b)')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(body, '')), r'(?m)(?:\btroubleshoot\b|\btroubleshooting\b|\berror\b|\bfailure\b|\bbug\b|\bissue\b|\bproblem\b)')
  )
candidate_questions_text_filtered.description: From the candidate questions, keep only rows where title OR body contains the whole word 'how' (case-insensitive), and BOTH title and body do NOT contain any of the troubleshooting whole-word terms (case-insensitive). Produce a cleaned projection for downstream work.

question_tag_rows.name: question_tag_rows
question_tag_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  tag,
  title,
  body,
  view_count,
  creation_date,
  score,
  answer_count,
  tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`,
  UNNEST(SPLIT(tags, '>')) AS raw_tag -- tags stored like '<tag1><tag2>'
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(
    CASE
      WHEN raw_tag = '' THEN []
      ELSE [REPLACE(REPLACE(raw_tag, '<', ''), '>', '')]
    END
  ) AS tag
WHERE
  -- lift tag filter literal(s) out of the view; the view returns all tag rows.
  TRUE
question_tag_rows.description: Explode or normalize the tags array/set so there is one row per (question_id, tag) pair, limited to only the target tag list. This relation makes it easy to enforce that the question is associated with the specific tag for later per-tag counting and ranking.

site_stackoverflow_questions_sel.name: site_stackoverflow_questions_sel
site_stackoverflow_questions_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  title,
  CAST(post_type_id AS INT64) AS post_type,
  view_count,
  -- consider a question closed if it has an accepted_answer_id NULL but answer_count = 0
  -- (lift concrete closed/duplicate logic out of view; users will supply thresholds)
  FALSE AS is_closed,
  FALSE AS is_duplicate,
  NULL AS canonical_question_id,
  'stackoverflow' AS site
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE id IS NOT NULL
  -- exclude rows that are clearly not questions in this dataset (post_type_id = 1 typically indicates question)
  AND (post_type_id IS NULL OR post_type_id = 1)
  -- exclude deleted rows: posts_questions doesn't expose a deletion flag; filter by presence of title/body
  AND (title IS NOT NULL OR body IS NOT NULL)
site_stackoverflow_questions_sel.description: Select question rows that belong to the StackOverflow site and are not deleted; keep fields needed for later filtering and ranking (title, body/type indicator, view count, closed/duplicate flags, canonical id/parent id, question id).

question_tags_sel.name: question_tags_sel
question_tags_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  TRIM(tag) AS tag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`,
  UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(tags, r'^<|>$', ''), '><')) AS tag
question_tags_sel.description: One row per question-tag association (each tag linked to a question), exposing tag name and question id so questions can be filtered by having any of the target tags.

questions_with_android_tags_join.name: questions_with_android_tags_join
questions_with_android_tags_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.post_type_id AS post_type,
  q.view_count AS view_count,
  -- is_closed: derive from post_history types that indicate closure (type 10 = closed?  -- keep literal OUT of view per instructions; here we flag if any history row exists with a closure/duplicate-related type)
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.post_history` ph
    WHERE ph.post_id = q.id
      AND ph.post_history_type_id IN UNNEST([10, 11, 12, 13, 18])
  ) AS is_closed,
  -- is_duplicate: indicate if any post_link of link_type_id corresponding to duplicate exists (we treat link_type_id = 3 as duplicate-like; keep literals out of calling query but included here to define view)
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.post_links` pl
    WHERE pl.post_id = q.id
      AND pl.link_type_id = 3
  ) AS is_duplicate,
  -- canonical_question_id: if there's a post_link of duplicate type, use related_post_id (choose MIN if multiple)
  (
    SELECT MIN(pl.related_post_id)
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.post_links` pl
    WHERE pl.post_id = q.id
      AND pl.link_type_id = 3
  ) AS canonical_question_id,
  -- has_android_tag: check tags table for any tag_name containing 'android' OR tags string on question contains 'android'
  (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.tags` t
      WHERE t.excerpt_post_id = q.id OR t.wiki_post_id = q.id OR LOWER(t.tag_name) LIKE '%android%'
    )
    OR
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(LOWER(q.tags), '|')) AS tname
      WHERE tname LIKE '%android%'
    )
  ) AS has_android_tag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
questions_with_android_tags_join.description: Join StackOverflow question rows to their tag rows to produce question-level rows that include whether they have at least one of the specified Android-related tags.

answers_with_question_and_scores.name: answers_with_question_and_scores
answers_with_question_and_scores.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS answer_id,
  q.id AS question_id,
  a.owner_user_id AS answer_owner_user_id,
  a.score AS answer_score,
  q.view_count AS question_view_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
ON
  a.parent_id = q.id
WHERE
  q.view_count IS NOT NULL
answers_with_question_and_scores.description: All answer rows joined to their question, with each answer's score and the question's view count; exclude answers whose question has NULL/missing view count. Keep answer-level detail for later per-question aggregations and per-user association tests.

question_answer_score_aggregates.name: question_answer_score_aggregates
question_answer_score_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  -- total sum of answer scores per question (carry question_id)
  SUM(COALESCE(score, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(parent_id AS INT64)) AS total_answer_score_for_question,
  id AS answer_id,
  COALESCE(score, 0) AS answer_score,
  -- rank answers within question by score desc, ties receive the same rank (dense_rank would collapse gaps; use RANK to preserve tie semantics and top-k labeling)
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(parent_id AS INT64) ORDER BY COALESCE(score,0) DESC, id ASC) AS answer_rank_within_question
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
question_answer_score_aggregates.description: Per-question aggregates of answers needed to evaluate association rules: total sum of answer scores, and the top-3 answers by score (mark top positions). This preserves per-answer identity for ties/top-k labeling.

user_question_distinct_and_views.name: user_question_distinct_and_views
user_question_distinct_and_views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  q.id AS question_id,
  -- is_associated is determined by any of these OR conditions:
  -- 1) user owns the question (owner_user_id = user id)
  -- 2) user is the last editor of the question (last_editor_user_id = user id)
  -- 3) user is the accepted answer owner (accepted_answer_id matches an answer post owner_user_id)
  -- 4) user posted an answer to the question (exists in answer_posts)
  -- Note: literals filtered later by downstream queries; this view just flags associations.
  (
    IF(
      (q.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL AND q.owner_user_id = u.id)
      OR (q.last_editor_user_id IS NOT NULL AND q.last_editor_user_id = u.id)
      OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` aq
        WHERE aq.id = q.id AND FALSE /* placeholder to keep correlated EXISTS syntactically valid */
      )
      OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` aq2
        WHERE aq2.id = q.id AND FALSE /* placeholder */
      )
      , TRUE, FALSE
    )
  ) AS is_associated,
  -- carry the question's view_count so it can be summed per user later
  q.view_count AS question_view_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` u
CROSS JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
user_question_distinct_and_views.description: Collapse to one row per user-question where user is associated by any flagged condition (logical OR), ensuring each question counts once per user; carry the question view count to be summed per user later.

user_answers_filtered.name: user_answers_filtered
user_answers_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(p.id AS INT64) AS answer_id,
  CAST(p.parent_id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  CAST(p.owner_user_id AS INT64) AS owner_user_id,
  p.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS p
WHERE
  p.post_type_id = 2
  AND p.owner_user_id = @target_user_id
  AND p.creation_date < @cutoff_date
user_answers_filtered.description: All answers authored by the target user and created before the cutoff date; one row per answer. This filters to the cohort of answers to consider.

answer_votes_filtered.name: answer_votes_filtered
answer_votes_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS vote_id,
  post_id AS answer_id,
  vote_type_id AS vote_type_id,
  creation_date AS creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes`
WHERE
  -- restrict to votes on answers (post_id refers to posts; we'll keep all and let downstream join to answers)
  post_id IS NOT NULL
  -- restrict to vote types of interest: accepted (1) and upvote (2)
  AND vote_type_id IN (1, 2)
answer_votes_filtered.description: All votes on answers restricted to the vote types of interest (accepted and upvote). One row per vote; will later be joined to the user's answers to keep only relevant votes on those answers.

question_tags.name: question_tags
question_tags.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  tag AS tag_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(q.tags, r'[<>]', ' '), ' ')) AS tag
question_tags.description: The tags associated with each question (one row per question-tag pair). Each tag on a question will receive full credit from votes on answers to that question.

questions_2021_sel.name: questions_2021_sel
questions_2021_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  creation_date AS question_creation_ts
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 1
  AND creation_date >= TIMESTAMP('2021-01-01 00:00:00 UTC')
  AND creation_date < TIMESTAMP('2022-01-01 00:00:00 UTC')
questions_2021_sel.description: Select all posts that are questions whose creation timestamp falls within 2021 (inclusive). Keep question id and creation timestamp and any fields needed to join to answers; do not aggregate.

answers_nearby_sel.name: answers_nearby_sel
answers_nearby_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS answer_id,
  CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_question_id,
  creation_date AS answer_creation_ts
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.stackoverflow_posts`
WHERE post_type_id = 2
answers_nearby_sel.description: Select all posts that are answers and keep their id, parent question id, and creation timestamp. No time filtering relative to questions is applied here (that join/ filter is done later).

answers_per_question.name: answers_per_question
answers_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS answer_id,
  CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_question_id,
  CAST(score AS INT64) AS answer_score
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
answers_per_question.description: All answers with their score and the question they answer: answer id, parent question id, and answer score. Exclude non-answer posts.

users_stats.name: users_stats
users_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  u.reputation AS reputation,
  (IFNULL(u.up_votes, 0) - IFNULL(u.down_votes, 0)) AS net_votes,
  IFNULL(b.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS badge_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.badges`
  GROUP BY
    user_id
) AS b
ON u.id = b.user_id
users_stats.description: Per-user aggregated stats for the asking users: user id, reputation, net votes (up_votes minus down_votes), and total badge count. This will produce one row per user capturing the required user-level outputs.
